activity.notes: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim led the Umayyad conquest of Sindh beginning in 711 and then administered the conquered province until his recall and death in 715. The mod exposes him to Sindh, Arabia and India, but historically he was an Umayyad commander and provincial governor, not a sovereign ruler of three separate civilizations.

sources.title: TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi — Muhammed b. Kāsım es-Sekafî
sources.citation_text: The TDV Encyclopaedia of Islam article treats Muhammad ibn al-Qasim as the Umayyad commander of the conquest of Sindh and cites the standard Encyclopaedia of Islam and specialist scholarship.

review_context.requested_identity: MUHAMMAD IBN AL-QASIM — SINDH, ARABIA, AND INDIA
review_context.correction_note: Bind military and provincial authority to the Umayyad Caliphate; do not invent sovereign rules over Arabia or India.
